commit_message:
[Merged] [wasm] Share import wrappers per WasmEngine

IOW, share them per process, instead of duplicating them for each
NativeModule. Detailed changes:

- The WasmImportWrapperCache is promoted from having an instance per
  NativeModule to having an instance per WasmEngine. It also gets its
  own code space for storing wrappers.
- Wrapper compilation functions now return a WasmCompilationResult
  instead of an already-published WasmCode, so that callers can decide
  where to put the WasmCode. That is done, specifically, by the
  WasmImportWrapperCache.
- WasmCode objects used for wrappers now don't have a NativeModule,
  i.e. their native_module_ == nullptr.
- Whereas wrappers previously had their lifetime implicitly tied to the
  NativeModule that owned them, we must now accurately track their
  refcount.
- To this end, WasmDispatchTables get an off-heap WasmDispatchTableData,
  which keeps track of all wrappers referenced by the table. Storing
  this information off-heap is necessary so that it's still available
  when the table's finalizer is invoked (at which time the table itself
  can no longer be accessed).

Using shared wrappers for WasmJSFunctions is left for a future patch.

pr_description:
Share compiled Wasm import wrappers across NativeModules through a process-wide cache with its own code space. Track wrapper references in off-heap dispatch-table data so their lifetime remains independent of any single NativeModule.

Track entry into code collection with an atomic dying flag on each WasmCode. Cache lookups hold scoped references and decline dying wrappers, while dispatch-table installation checks that wrappers remain eligible for use. Stack lookups retain visibility of dying code until its remaining activations finish, and the engine no longer needs a separate dead-code set.

ground_truth.reason: This PR includes the feature with the fix already applied, so the vulnerability is not present

[wasm] Replace {dead_code_} set with {is_dying_} bit

This saves some memory, and fixes a bug.

agent_reasoning: The shared cache could otherwise return a wrapper that had already entered code GC, allowing a dispatch table to retain a pointer to code destined for reclamation. The edits replace the engine dead_code_ set with a permanent atomic dying flag and reject dying objects after acquiring scoped references. In this older snapshot, ModificationScope::operator[] covers the compilation-time cache recheck, and both inline FindWrapper callers acquire the cache lock and scoped references; dispatch-table Add rejects dying wrappers. Lookup continues to expose dying code for stack scanning. Only the five source files touched by the supplied change were edited; tests were untouched. git diff --check and validate_pr_state passed; no build or runtime tests were run.
